transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hello. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I've been having this issue when people talk to me. Like, people at the museum will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’ll be looking right at them... but then I realize I completely missed the middle part of what they just said. I always have to stop and ask them to run it by me again. It's been happening enough that I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with paying attention?

It's been noticeably causing trouble for, oh, about two years and four months now. That was right around the time a good friend of mine passed away, and I ended up having to take over the museum liaison duties all by myself.
Over these past two years, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or depressed most days?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, losing my friend was tough, of course, but... no, I haven't been feeling depressed or down most days. My mood has been pretty normal, really. It's just this problem with losing my focus that's been bothering me.
Did you have similar difficulties with attention or focus when you were a child or in school?

Yeah, actually, I did. I remember... well, even back in grade school, my report cards always said things about how I daydreamed a lot, or that I needed reminders to finish my work. My mother actually used to have to sit right beside me at the table just to keep me on track with my homework. That was before I was twelve or so. So, yes, I guess it was an issue back then, too.
Do these difficulties with attention also affect your day-to-day life at home, outside of work?

Well, I wouldn't really say it causes much trouble at home. At work, sure, with all the museum stuff, but around the house... no, I haven't really noticed it being an issue. I mean, my day-to-day routine at home is pretty simple, so there's not much to lose track of, you know?
